content.value_statement: Architecture documentation often becomes incomplete as codebases grow. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a C4 documentation workflow.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes repository directories from deepest folders upward to build code-level C4 documentation.
Synthesizes code documentation into component, container, and context views.
Creates Mermaid C4 diagrams for components, containers, and system context.
Documents APIs and can outline OpenAPI specifications for container interfaces.
Writes a C4-Documentation directory with linked Markdown files.
limitations: Requires access to the target repository files to produce useful documentation.
Generated diagrams and component boundaries need human review for architecture accuracy.
Large repositories may require multiple passes to avoid incomplete coverage.
It does not deploy systems or verify runtime behavior.

use_cases.title: Onboard Developers
use_cases.description: Create a navigable C4 documentation set so new contributors can understand code structure and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Prepare Architecture Reviews
use_cases.description: Map components, containers, and external systems before a design review or modernization effort.

use_cases.title: Document Service Interfaces
use_cases.description: Identify container interfaces and prepare OpenAPI outlines for service consumers.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Default C4 Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create C4 documentation for this repository. Use the default C4-Documentation output folder and include code, component, container, and context levels.

prompt_templates.title: Focus On Selected Folders
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the src and services directories only. Exclude tests and generated files. Produce component and container documentation with Mermaid diagrams.

prompt_templates.title: Map Microservice Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate C4 documentation for a microservice repo. Emphasize deployment units, APIs, external dependencies, and OpenAPI outlines for each container.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing C4 Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Review existing C4-Documentation output, find gaps against the repository, and update missing relationships, personas, APIs, and diagram links.

output_examples.input: Document a new web application repository.
output: A C4-Documentation folder with code-level pages, component summaries, container views, and a system context overview.
Mermaid diagrams show key relationships between users, containers, components, and external systems.

output_examples.input: Create architecture docs for a service with APIs.
output: Container documentation lists service APIs, protocols, dependencies, and deployment details.
API specification notes describe endpoints, request models, responses, authentication, and error cases.

best_practices: Run it after dependencies and project structure are available.
Review generated boundaries with engineers who own the system.
Keep generated documentation with source control changes when architecture changes.
anti_patterns: Do not run it on unrelated repositories or partial file exports.
Do not publish generated architecture docs without checking private system details.
Do not treat generated API specs as canonical without endpoint validation.

faq.question: Does this skill create all four C4 levels?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides code, component, container, and context documentation, although teams can choose the levels they need.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No. The instructions reference C4 documentation links but do not require network calls to generate files.

faq.question: Where are files written?
faq.answer: The workflow writes Markdown and API documentation under C4-Documentation in the repository root by default.

faq.question: Can it document APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the assistant to identify container interfaces and prepare OpenAPI-style specifications.

faq.question: Will it modify application code?
faq.answer: No. The described workflow creates documentation files and does not ask to change application source code.

faq.question: Who should review the output?
faq.answer: Engineers, architects, and service owners should review diagrams, dependencies, and API descriptions for accuracy.
